510:         if operand.kind() == "function_call" {
511:             if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(operand, source) {
512:                 if name == "isempty" {
513:                     // Check if the argument to isempty is strfind(...)
514:                     if let Some(args_node) = find_arguments(operand) {
515:                         if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
516:                             if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
517:                                 if let Some(inner_name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
518:                                     if inner_name == "strfind" {
519:                                         diags.push(make_diag("STCCS", node));
520:                                     }
521:                                 }
522:                             }
523:                         }
524:                     }
525:                 }
526:             }
527:         }
528: 
529:         diags
530:     }
531: 
532:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
533:     // File-level checks: AGROW, SAGROW, PFBNS
534:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
535: 
536:     /// File-level check for array/struct growth inside loops.
537:     fn check_growth_in_loops(
538:         &self,
539:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
540:         source: &str,
541:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
542:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
543:         let root = tree.root_node();
544:         self.traverse_for_growth(&root, source, false, &mut diags);
545:         diags
546:     }
547: 
548:     /// Recursive traversal looking for growth patterns inside loops.
549:     fn traverse_for_growth(
550:         &self,
551:         node: &tree_sitter::Node,
552:         source: &str,
553:         in_loop: bool,
554:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
555:     ) {
556:         let kind = node.kind();
557:         let entering_loop = kind == "for_statement" || kind == "while_statement";
558:         let now_in_loop = in_loop || entering_loop;
559: 
560:         // Only check assignment nodes inside loops.
561:         if now_in_loop && kind == "assignment" {
562:             self.check_assignment_growth(*node, source, diags);
563:         }
564: 
565:         // Also detect growth via full-node text for assignments that tree-sitter
566:         // may parse differently (e.g., s.field(end+1) = k might parse as
567:         // a function_call at statement level rather than an assignment).
568:         if now_in_loop
569:             && (kind == "function_call" || kind == "cell_index")
570:             && is_statement_level(node)
571:         {
572:             let text = node_text(*node, source);
573:             let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
574:             if normalized.contains("end+1") {
575:                 let has_dot = text.contains('.');
576:                 let check_id = if has_dot { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
577:                 if self.is_enabled(check_id) {
578:                     diags.push(make_diag(check_id, *node));
579:                 }
580:             }
581:         }
582: 
583:         let count = node.child_count();
584:         for i in 0..count {
585:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
586:                 self.traverse_for_growth(&child, source, now_in_loop, diags);
587:             }
588:         }
589:     }
590: 
591:     /// Check a single assignment node for growth patterns.
592:     ///
593:     /// Detects:
594:     /// 1. `x = [x, val]` or `x = [x; val]` — concatenation growth (AGROW)
595:     /// 2. `x(end+1) = val` — end+1 indexing (AGROW)
596:     /// 3. `x{end+1} = val` — cell growth (AGROW)
597:     /// 4. `s.field(end+1) = val` — struct field growth (SAGROW)
598:     /// 5. `x = []` followed by growth — PFBNS (simplified: flag end+1 patterns)
599:     fn check_assignment_growth(
600:         &self,
601:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
602:         source: &str,
603:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
604:     ) {
605:         let lhs = match node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
606:             Some(n) => n,
607:             None => return,
608:         };
609:         let rhs = match node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2)) {
610:             Some(n) => n,
611:             None => return,
612:         };
613: 
614:         let lhs_text = node_text(lhs, source);
615:         let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
616: 
617:         // Determine if LHS involves a struct field (for SAGROW vs AGROW).
618:         let is_struct = lhs.kind() == "field_expression"
619:             || (lhs.kind() == "function_call" && lhs_text.contains('.'));
620: 
621:         let check_id = if is_struct { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
622: 
623:         if !self.is_enabled(check_id) {
624:             return;
625:         }
626: 
627:         // Pattern 1: x(end+1) = ... or x{end+1} = ...
628:         // LHS is a function_call (indexing) or cell_index containing "end+1"
629:         // or "end + 1".
630:         if (lhs.kind() == "function_call" || lhs.kind() == "cell_index")
631:             && contains_end_plus_pattern(lhs, source)
632:         {
633:             diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
634:             return;
635:         }
636: 
637:         // Pattern 1b: s.field(end+1) = ... — may parse with field_expression as LHS
638:         // and end+1 in the assignment text before the `=`.
639:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
640:             // Check the full assignment text up to the `=` for end+1 pattern.
641:             let assign_text = node_text(node, source);
642:             if let Some(eq_pos) = assign_text.find('=') {
643:                 let lhs_full = &assign_text[..eq_pos];
644:                 let normalized: String = lhs_full.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
645:                 if normalized.contains("end+1") {
646:                     diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
647:                     return;
648:                 }
649:             }
650:         }
651: 
652:         // Pattern 2: x = [x, val] or x = [x; val]
653:         // LHS is a simple identifier, RHS is a matrix containing that identifier.
654:         if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
655:             let var_name = lhs_text;
656:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
657:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
658:                 return;
659:             }
660:             // Also check cell: x = {x, val} — though less common
661:             if rhs.kind() == "cell" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
662:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
663:                 return;
664:             }
665:         }
666: 
667:         // Pattern 3: s.field = [s.field, val]
668:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
669:             let field_text = lhs_text;
670:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && rhs_text.contains(field_text) {
671:                 diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
672:             }
673:         }
674:     }
675: }

688:     }

709:                 diags.extend(self.check_boolean_context_binary(ctx.node, ctx.source));

763: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
764: // Helper: node text extraction
765: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
766: 
767: /// Extract the raw text of a node.
768: fn node_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
769:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
770: }
771: 
772: /// Extract function name from a `function_call` node.
773: fn extract_func_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
774:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
775:         return None;
776:     }
777:     let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
778:     Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
779: }
780: 
781: /// Extract command name from a `command` node.
782: fn extract_command_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
783:     if node.kind() != "command" {
784:         return None;
785:     }
786:     let name_node = node.child(0)?;
787:     if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
788:         Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
789:     } else {
790:         None
791:     }
792: }
793: 
794: /// Extract command arguments as a list of text fragments.
795: fn extract_command_args<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Vec<&'a str> {
796:     let mut args = Vec::new();
797:     let count = node.child_count();
798:     for i in 0..count {
799:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
800:             // Skip the command_name (first child) and punctuation.
801:             if child.kind() == "command_name" || child.kind() == ";" || child.kind() == "," {
802:                 continue;
803:             }
804:             let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
805:             if !text.is_empty() {
806:                 args.push(text);
807:             }
808:         }
809:     }
810:     args
811: }
812: 
813: /// Extract the operator text from a `binary_operator` or `boolean_operator`.
814: fn extract_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
815:     // The operator is typically the second child (between left and right operands),
816:     // or we can scan children for the operator token.
817:     let count = node.child_count();
818:     for i in 0..count {
819:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
820:             let text = node_text(child, source);
821:             // Operator tokens are short and not identifiers/expressions.
822:             match text {
823:                 "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "\\" | "^" | ".*" | "./" | ".\\" | ".^" | "&" | "|"
824:                 | "&&" | "||" | "==" | "~=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" => return text,
825:                 _ => continue,
826:             }
827:         }
828:     }
829:     ""
830: }
831: 
832: /// Extract the operator text from a `unary_operator` node.
833: fn extract_unary_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
834:     if let Some(child) = node.child(0) {
835:         let text = node_text(child, source);
836:         match text {
837:             "~" | "-" | "+" | "!" => return text,
838:             _ => {}
839:         }
840:     }
841:     ""
842: }
843: 
844: /// Get the first named child of a node.
845: fn first_named_child(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
846:     let count = node.named_child_count();
847:     if count > 0 {
848:         node.named_child(0)
849:     } else {
850:         None
851:     }
852: }
853: 
854: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
855: // Helper: argument analysis
856: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
857: 
858: /// Count the number of arguments in a `function_call` node.
859: fn count_args(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> usize {
860:     // Arguments are in the `arguments` child node.
861:     match find_arguments(node) {
862:         Some(args_node) => args_node.named_child_count(),
863:         None => 0,
864:     }
865: }
866: 
867: /// Find the `arguments` child node of a `function_call` node.
868: ///
869: /// tree-sitter-matlab does not attach a field name to this child, so the
870: /// arguments list is located by node kind.
871: fn find_arguments<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node<'a>> {
872:     let count = node.child_count();
873:     for i in 0..count {
874:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
875:             if child.kind() == "arguments" {
876:                 return Some(child);
877:             }
878:         }
879:     }
880:     None
881: }
882: 
883: /// Check if a function_call has a specific string argument.
884: fn has_string_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, value: &str) -> bool {
885:     let count = node.child_count();
886:     for i in 0..count {
887:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
888:             let text = node_text(child, source);
889:             // Match quoted strings: 'value' or "value"
890:             let trimmed = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
891:             if trimmed.eq_ignore_ascii_case(value) {
892:                 return true;
893:             }
894:             // Recurse into arguments node.
895:             if child.kind() == "arguments" && has_string_arg(child, source, value) {
896:                 return true;
897:             }
898:         }
899:     }
900:     false
901: }
902: 
903: /// Check if `exist(...)` has a second argument indicating type ('file', 'dir', etc.).
904: fn has_exist_type_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
905:     // exist should have 2 arguments, with the second being a string like 'file', 'dir'.
906:     let arg_count = count_args(node);
907:     if arg_count < 2 {
908:         return false;
909:     }
910:     has_string_arg(node, source, "file")
911:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "dir")
912:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "builtin")
913:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "class")
914: }
915: 
916: /// Check if a regexp/regexpi call has an overly simple pattern (just alphanumeric).
917: fn has_simple_regex_pattern(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
918:     // Look for the second argument (the pattern) and check if it's purely alphanumeric
919:     // (meaning a simple `contains` or `strcmp` would suffice).
920:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
921:         Some(n) => n,
922:         None => return false,
923:     };
924: 
925:     // The pattern is usually the 2nd argument.
926:     let named_count = args_node.named_child_count();
927:     if named_count < 2 {
928:         return false;
929:     }
930: 
931:     if let Some(pattern_node) = args_node.named_child(1) {
932:         let text = node_text(pattern_node, source);
933:         // Strip quotes.
934:         let inner = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
935:         // If the pattern is purely alphanumeric (no regex metacharacters), it's simple.
936:         if !inner.is_empty() && inner.chars().all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_') {
937:             return true;
938:         }
939:     }
940:     false
941: }
942: 
943: /// Check if the first argument to lower/upper is a strcmp call (STNCI pattern).
944: fn has_strcmp_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
945:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
946:         Some(n) => n,
947:         None => return false,
948:     };
949: 
950:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
951:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
952:             if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
953:                 return name == "strcmp" || name == "strcmpi";
954:             }
955:         }
956:     }
957:     false
958: }
959: 
960: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
961: // Helper: pattern detection
962: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
963: 
964: /// Check if the function_call is a nested call of the same function.
965: /// e.g., max(max(x)) — the outer call's first argument is the same function.
966: fn is_nested_same_call(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, func_name: &str) -> bool {
967:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
968:         Some(n) => n,
969:         None => return false,
970:     };
971: 
972:     // Check if first argument is a function_call with the same name.
973:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
974:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
975:             if let Some(inner_name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
976:                 return inner_name == func_name;
977:             }
978:         }
979:     }
980:     false
981: }
982: 
983: /// Check if a function_call node is used as a subscript index.
984: /// i.e., the parent is the arguments of another function_call.
985: fn is_subscript_context(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
986:     if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
987:         // Direct parent might be `arguments` of a function_call.
988:         if parent.kind() == "arguments" {
989:             if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
990:                 return grandparent.kind() == "function_call";
991:             }
992:         }
993:         // Or the parent is directly a function_call (as an argument).
994:         if parent.kind() == "function_call" {
995:             // Make sure this node is not the function name itself.
996:             if let Some(name_node) = parent.child_by_field_name("name") {
997:                 return name_node.id() != node.id();
998:             }
999:         }
1000:     }
1001:     false
1002: }
1003: 
1004: /// Check if a node is at statement level (direct child of source_file or block).
1005: fn is_statement_level(node: &tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1006:     node.parent()
1007:         .map(|p| matches!(p.kind(), "source_file" | "block"))
1008:         .unwrap_or(false)
1009: }
1010: 
1011: /// Check if node is inside a loop (for_statement or while_statement).
1012: fn is_inside_loop(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1013:     let mut current = node.parent();
1014:     while let Some(p) = current {
1015:         match p.kind() {
1016:             "for_statement" | "while_statement" => return true,
1017:             "function_definition" => return false, // Stop at function boundary.
1018:             _ => {}
1019:         }
1020:         current = p.parent();
1021:     }
1022:     false
1023: }
1024: 
1025: /// Check if a node is inside a condition expression (if/while/elseif).
1026: fn is_in_condition(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1027:     let mut current = node.parent();
1028:     while let Some(p) = current {
1029:         match p.kind() {
1030:             "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "elseif_clause" => {
1031:                 // Check if our node is in the condition part, not the body.
1032:                 // The condition is typically the first expression child after the keyword.
1033:                 if let Some(cond) = p.child_by_field_name("condition") {
1034:                     return is_descendant_of(node, cond);
1035:                 }
1036:                 // Fallback: check if node appears before the "block" child.
1037:                 let count = p.child_count();
1038:                 for i in 0..count {
1039:                     if let Some(child) = p.child(i) {
1040:                         if child.kind() == "block" {
1041:                             // If node is before the block, it's in the condition.
1042:                             return node.start_byte() < child.start_byte();
1043:                         }
1044:                     }
1045:                 }
1046:                 return true;
1047:             }
1048:             "function_definition" => return false,
1049:             _ => {}
1050:         }
1051:         current = p.parent();
1052:     }
1053:     false
1054: }
1055: 
1056: /// Check if `needle` is a descendant of `haystack`.
1057: fn is_descendant_of(needle: tree_sitter::Node, haystack: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1058:     needle.start_byte() >= haystack.start_byte() && needle.end_byte() <= haystack.end_byte()
1059: }
1060: 
1061: /// Check if an `inv()` call is an operand of a binary_operator.
1062: fn has_inv_operand(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
1063:     let count = node.child_count();
1064:     for i in 0..count {
1065:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
1066:             if child.kind() == "function_call" {
1067:                 if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(child, source) {
1068:                     if name == "inv" {
1069:                         return true;
1070:                     }
1071:                 }
1072:             }
1073:         }
1074:     }
1075:     false
1076: }
1077: 
1078: /// Check if both operands of a binary_operator are the same text.
1079: fn has_same_operands(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
1080:     // Typically: child(0) = left, child(1) = op, child(2) = right.
1081:     let left = match node.child(0) {
1082:         Some(n) => n,
1083:         None => return false,
1084:     };
1085:     let right = match node.child(2) {
1086:         Some(n) => n,
1087:         None => return false,
1088:     };
1089:     let left_text = node_text(left, source).trim();
1090:     let right_text = node_text(right, source).trim();
1091:     !left_text.is_empty() && left_text == right_text
1092: }
1093: 
1094: /// Check if an indexing expression contains `end+1` or `end + 1` pattern.

1103: fn matrix_contains_var(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, var_name: &str) -> bool {
1104:     // Walk the matrix's children looking for an identifier matching var_name.
1105:     let count = node.child_count();
1106:     for i in 0..count {
1107:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
1108:             if child.kind() == "identifier" && node_text(child, source) == var_name {
1109:                 return true;
1110:             }
1111:             // Recurse into rows.
1112:             if child.kind() == "row" && matrix_contains_var(child, source, var_name) {
1113:                 return true;

1115:         }

1125: ) -> Option<(&'a str, &'a str)> {
1126:     // comparison_operator children: left op right

1128:     let op_node = node.child(1)?;
1129:     let right = node.child(2)?;
1130:

1137:     if left.kind() == "function_call" {

1: //! Shared utilities for rule-module unit tests.
2: //!
3: //! These helpers mirror the `Linter` dispatch so tests can exercise both
4: //! node-level (`check`) and file-level (`check_file`) rules directly,
5: //! without going through the full CLI.

9: use mlt_core::{Diagnostic, FileContext, NodeContext, Rule};
10: use tree_sitter::{Node, Parser};
11: 
12: /// Parse MATLAB source and return the tree.
13: pub fn parse(source: &str) -> tree_sitter::Tree {
14:     let mut parser = Parser::new();
15:     parser
16:         .set_language(&tree_sitter_matlab::LANGUAGE.into())
17:         .expect("failed to load tree-sitter-matlab");
18:     parser.parse(source, None).expect("parse failed")
19: }
20: 
21: /// Build a `FileContext` with a fixed test file path.
22: pub fn file_ctx<'a>(tree: &'a tree_sitter::Tree, source: &'a str) -> FileContext<'a> {
23:     FileContext {
24:         tree,
25:         source,
26:         file_path: std::path::Path::new("test.m"),
27:     }
28: }
29: 
30: /// Run a rule's node-level `check()` over every node in the tree, mimicking
31: /// the Linter's depth-first dispatch. Returns all diagnostics.
32: pub fn lint_nodes(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
33:     let tree = parse(source);
34:     let path = std::path::Path::new("test.m");
35:     let targets: Vec<&str> = rule.target_node_types().to_vec();
36:     let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
37: 
38:     fn walk(
39:         node: Node,
40:         source: &str,
41:         path: &std::path::Path,
42:         targets: &[&str],
43:         rule: &dyn Rule,
44:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
45:     ) {
46:         if targets.contains(&node.kind()) {
47:             let ctx = NodeContext {
48:                 node,
49:                 source,
50:                 file_path: path,
51:             };
52:             diagnostics.extend(rule.check(&ctx));
53:         }
54:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
55:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
56:             walk(child, source, path, targets, rule, diagnostics);
57:         }
58:     }
59: 
60:     walk(tree.root_node(), source, path, &targets, rule, &mut diagnostics);
61:     diagnostics
62: }
63: 
64: /// Run a rule's file-level `check_file()`. Returns all diagnostics.
65: pub fn lint_file(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
66:     let tree = parse(source);
67:     let ctx = file_ctx(&tree, source);
68:     rule.check_file(&ctx)
69: }
70: 
71: /// Returns true if any diagnostic has the given rule ID.
72: pub fn has_id(diags: &[Diagnostic], id: &str) -> bool {
73:     diags.iter().any(|d| d.rule_id == id)
74: }

"""Mechanically split performance.rs into performance/ directory modules."""
import pathlib, re

ROOT = pathlib.Path("/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt")
SRC = ROOT / "crates/mlt_rules/src/performance.rs"
OUT = ROOT / "crates/mlt_rules/src/performance"

text = SRC.read_text()
lines = text.split("\n")
n = len(lines)

def line(idx):
    return lines[idx]

def find_close(start, pattern):
    """Find first line index >= start matching `pattern`."""
    for i in range(start, n):
        if re.match(pattern, lines[i]):
            return i
    raise RuntimeError(f"no close for start {start}")

# ---------------- Extract methods from the impl block ----------------

    if m:

    if lines[i].startswith("impl Rule for"):
        break

for i, name in method_starts:
    close = find_close(i + 1, r"^    }$")
    impl_methods[name] = lines[i:close + 1]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mechanically split crates/mlt_rules/src/performance.rs into a directory of
one-file-per-check modules under crates/mlt_rules/src/performance/.

Pure mechanical refactor: method bodies and test bodies are copied byte-for-byte
from the original; the only edits are `pub(crate)` visibility additions and
module scaffolding.
"""
import pathlib
import re

ROOT = pathlib.Path("/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt")
SRC = ROOT / "crates/mlt_rules/src/performance.rs"
OUT = ROOT / "crates/mlt_rules/src/performance"

text = SRC.read_text()
lines = text.split("\n")
n = len(lines)


def find_close(start: int, pattern: str) -> int:
    """First line index >= start matching `pattern`."""
    rx = re.compile(pattern)
    for i in range(start, n):
        if rx.match(lines[i]):
            return i
    raise RuntimeError(f"no close for start line {start}")


def extract_range(start: int, end: int, what: str) -> str:
    """Lines [start, end] inclusive joined by newlines; sanity-balance braces."""
    block = "\n".join(lines[start:end + 1])
    if block.count("{") != block.count("}"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"unbalanced braces in {what} (lines {start}..{end})")
    return block


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Methods inside `impl PerformanceEngine { ... }`
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
impl_start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l == "impl PerformanceEngine {")
impl_rule_start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l == "impl Rule for PerformanceEngine {")

method_starts = []
for i in range(impl_start + 1, impl_rule_start):
    m = re.match(r"^    (pub )?fn (\w+)", lines[i])
    if m:
        method_starts.append((i, m.group(1)))

impl_methods = {}  # name -> body text (lines joined)
for i, name in method_starts:
    close = find_close(i + 1, r"^    }$")
    impl_methods[name] = extract_range(i, close, f"method {name}")
    # advance past the method so nested `    fn` (none) aren't missed
    if close >= impl_rule_start:
        raise RuntimeError(f"method {name} ran past impl block")

KEPT_METHODS = [
    "from_config",
    "is_enabled",
    "check_growth_in_loops",
    "traverse_for_growth",
    "check_assignment_growth",
]
MOVED_METHODS = [
    "check_function_call",
    "check_command",
    "check_binary_operator",
    "check_boolean_context_binary",
    "check_comparison",
    "check_unary",
]
for name in KEPT_METHODS + MOVED_METHODS:
    if name not in impl_methods:
        raise RuntimeError(f"missing method {name}")
missing = set(impl_methods) - set(KEPT_METHODS) - set(MOVED_METHODS)
if missing:
    raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected methods: {missing}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Free helpers (column-0 `fn ...`)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
helper_starts = []
for i in range(n):
    m = re.match(r"^fn (\w+)", lines[i])
    if m:
        helper_starts.append((i, m.group(1)))

helpers = {}  # name -> body text
for i, name in helper_starts:
    close = find_close(i + 1, r"^}$")
    helpers[name] = extract_range(i, close, f"helper {name}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fixed scaffolding slices (1-based line numbers from the original)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sl(a: int, b: int) -> str:
    """Lines a..b inclusive (1-based) joined by newlines."""
    return extract_range(a - 1, b - 1, f"lines {a}..{b}")

MODULE_DOC = sl(1, 36)
USES = sl(38, 39)
CONFIG_SECTION = sl(41, 53)
METADATA_HEADER = sl(55, 57)
CHECK_META_AND_CHECKS = sl(59, 108)
RULE_HEADER = sl(119, 121)
ENGINE_STRUCT = sl(123, 130)
TARGET_NODES = sl(132, 140)
RULE_IMPL = sl(677, 725)
HELPERS_HEADER = sl(727, 729)
INVENTORY_SECTION = sl(1202, 1209)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
tests_mod_start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l == "mod tests {")

test_entries = []  # (start, end_inclusive, name, section_comment_or_None)
test_re = re.compile(r"^    fn (\w+)")
attr_line = None
cur_section = None
i = tests_mod_start + 1
while i < n:
    l = lines[i]
    if l == "    #[test]":
        attr_line = i
    m = test_re.match(l)
    if m and m.group(1) != "engine":
        name = m.group(1)
        close = find_close(i + 1, r"^    }$")
        start = attr_line if attr_line is not None else i
        block = extract_range(start, close, f"test {name}")
        test_entries.append((start, close, name, cur_section, block))
        attr_line = None
        i = close + 1
        continue
    if re.match(r"^    // --", l):
        cur_section = l
    i += 1

all_test_names = [t[2] for t in test_entries]
print(f"total tests extracted: {len(all_test_names)}")

TEST_DEST = {
    "check_function_call.rs": [
        "gfld_fires_on_getfield", "gfld_not_fire_on_dot_access",
        "sfld_fires_on_setfield", "sfld_not_fire_on_dot_assignment",
        "exist_fires_with_type_argument", "exist_not_fire_without_type_argument",
        "st2nm_fires_on_str2num", "st2nm_not_fire_on_str2double",
        "flpst_fires_on_flipud", "flpst_fires_on_fliplr", "flpst_not_fire_on_flip",

def tests_module(dest_tests, use_lint_file=False):
    """Build the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` for a destination file."""
    used = set()
    for t in dest_tests:
        block = t[4]
        if "lint_file" in block:
            used.add("lint_file")
        if "lint_nodes" in block:
            used.add("lint_nodes")
        if "has_id" in block:
            used.add("has_id")
    test_util_import = "use crate::test_util::{" + ", ".join(sorted(used)) + "};"
    head = [
        "#[cfg(test)]",
        "mod tests {",
        f"    use super::super::test_support::engine;",
        f"    {test_util_import}",
        "",
    ]
    body = []
    prev_section = None
    for t in dest_tests:
        _, _, _, section, block = t
        if section is not None and section != prev_section:
            body.append(section)
            body.append("")
        body.append(block)
        prev_section = section
    tail = ["}"]
    return "\n".join(head + body + tail)


def emit_check_file(file_name, method_name, dest_tests):
    doc = f"//! {CHECK_DOCS[file_name]}"
    method = impl_methods[method_name]
    first = method.split("\n", 1)[0]
    assert re.match(r"^    fn check_", first), f"unexpected method start: {first!r}"

188:         source: &str,
189:         in_loop: bool,
190:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
191:     ) {

193:         let entering_loop = kind == "for_statement" || kind == "while_statement";
194:         let now_in_loop = in_loop || entering_loop;
195: 
196:         // Only check assignment nodes inside loops.
197:         if now_in_loop && kind == "assignment" {
198:             self.check_assignment_growth(*node, source, diags);
199:         }

201:         // Also detect growth via full-node text for assignments that tree-sitter
202:         // may parse differently (e.g., s.field(end+1) = k might parse as
203:         // a function_call at statement level rather than an assignment).
204:         if now_in_loop

206:             && is_statement_level(node)

208:             let text = node_text(*node, source);
209:             let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();

212:                 let check_id = if has_dot { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
213:                 if self.is_enabled(check_id) {

217:         }

220:         for i in 0..count {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verification for the mechanical performance.rs split.

Checks:
 1. Every moved method body is byte-identical to the original except the
    `pub(crate) ` visibility keyword on the `fn` line.
 2. Every kept method and free helper in mod.rs is byte-identical to the
    original except `pub(crate) ` on helper `fn` lines.
 3. Every check ID's implementation lives in exactly one file.
 4. Dispatch references in mod.rs match the moved method names.
 5. Moved-test count matches (81 total = 7 kept + 74 moved) and test bodies
    are byte-identical.
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path("/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt")
ORIG = ROOT / "crates/mlt_rules/src/performance.rs"
PERF = ROOT / "crates/mlt_rules/src/performance"

orig_lines = ORIG.read_text().split("\n")
n = len(orig_lines)
failures = []


def fail(msg):
    failures.append(msg)


def find_close(start, pattern):
    rx = re.compile(pattern)
    for i in range(start, n):
        if rx.match(orig_lines[i]):
            return i
    raise RuntimeError(f"no close {pattern} from {start}")


def extract_method(name):
    """Original text of a method (doc + fn + body)."""
    for i, l in enumerate(orig_lines):
        if re.match(rf"^    (pub )?fn {re.escape(name)}\b", l):
            close = find_close(i + 1, r"^    }$")
            doc = []
            j = i - 1
            while j >= 0 and orig_lines[j].lstrip().startswith("///"):
                doc.append(orig_lines[j])
                j -= 1
            doc.reverse()
            return "\n".join(doc + ["\n".join(orig_lines[i:close + 1])])
    raise RuntimeError(f"method {name} not found in original")


def extract_helper(name):
    for i, l in enumerate(orig_lines):
        if re.match(rf"^fn {re.escape(name)}\b", l):
            close = find_close(i + 1, r"^}$")
            doc = []
            j = i - 1
            while j >= 0 and orig_lines[j].lstrip().startswith("///"):
                doc.append(orig_lines[j])
                j -= 1
            doc.reverse()
            return "\n".join(doc + ["\n".join(orig_lines[i:close + 1])])
    raise RuntimeError(f"helper {name} not found in original")


def method_from_file(path, name):
    text = path.read_text()
    m = re.search(
        rf"(//!.*\n)*\n*(?P<body>    (pub\(crate\) )?fn {re.escape(name)}\b.*?\n    }})",
        text, re.DOTALL,
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    body = m.group("body")
    # strip the doc comments attached inside the file for pure-body comparison
    return body


MOVED = {
    "check_function_call": "check_function_call.rs",
    "check_command": "check_command.rs",
    "check_binary_operator": "check_binary_operator.rs",
    "check_boolean_context_binary": "check_boolean_context_binary.rs",
    "check_comparison": "check_comparison.rs",
    "check_unary": "check_unary.rs",
}
KEPT = ["from_config", "is_enabled", "check_growth_in_loops",
        "traverse_for_growth", "check_assignment_growth"]

# ---- 1. moved method bodies -------------------------------------------------
print("== moved method body diffs ==")
for name, fname in MOVED.items():
    orig = extract_method(name)
    new = method_from_file(PERF / fname, name)
    if new is None:
        fail(f"{fname}: method {name} not found")
        continue
    # normalize: remove pub(crate) keyword
    new_norm = new.replace("    pub(crate) fn ", "    fn ", 1)
    # also strip the `//!` module doc line of the file (not part of the method)
    if new_norm != orig:
        # print a focused diff
        import difflib
        diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(
            orig.split("\n"), new_norm.split("\n"),
            fromfile=f"original {name}", tofile=f"new {fname}", lineterm="",
        ))
        fail(f"{fname}: method {name} differs:\n" + "\n".join(diff[:40]))
        print(f"  {fname}: DIFFERS")
    else:
        print(f"  {fname}: identical (modulo `pub(crate)`)")

# ---- 2. kept methods --------------------------------------------------------
print("== kept method body diffs ==")
mod_text = (PERF / "mod.rs").read_text()
for name in KEPT:
    orig = extract_method(name)
    if orig not in mod_text:
        fail(f"mod.rs: kept method {name} differs or missing")
        print(f"  {name}: MISSING/DIFFERS")
    else:
        print(f"  {name}: present verbatim")

# ---- 3. free helpers --------------------------------------------------------
helper_names = []
for i, l in enumerate(orig_lines):
    if re.match(r"^fn (\w+)", l):
        helper_names.append(re.match(r"^fn (\w+)", l).group(1))
print("== free helper diffs ==")
for hname in helper_names:
    orig = extract_helper(hname)
    new = hname
    # find in mod.rs: compare normalized (strip pub(crate))
    # extract the helper from mod.rs
    m = re.search(
        rf"(?P<body>(pub\(crate\) )?fn {re.escape(hname)}\b.*?\n}})",
        mod_text, re.DOTALL,
    )
    if not m:
        fail(f"mod.rs: helper {hname} not found")
        print(f"  {hname}: MISSING")
        continue
    body = m.group("body")
    body_norm = body.replace("pub(crate) fn ", "fn ", 1)
    if body_norm != orig:
        import difflib
        diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(
            orig.split("\n"), body_norm.split("\n"),
            fromfile=f"original {hname}", tofile="mod.rs", lineterm="",
        ))
        fail(f"mod.rs: helper {hname} differs:\n" + "\n".join(diff[:40]))
        print(f"  {hname}: DIFFERS")
    else:
        print(f"  {hname}: identical (modulo `pub(crate)`)")


# ---- 4. dispatch references -------------------------------------------------
print("== dispatch references ==")
dispatch_refs = ["check_function_call", "check_command", "check_binary_operator",
                 "check_boolean_context_binary", "check_comparison", "check_unary",
                 "check_growth_in_loops"]
for ref in dispatch_refs:
    count = len(re.findall(rf"\bself\.{re.escape(ref)}\b", mod_text))
    print(f"  self.{ref}: {count} reference(s) in mod.rs dispatch")
    if count < 1:
        fail(f"dispatch missing self.{ref}")
# each moved method must be defined pub(crate) in exactly one check file
for name, fname in MOVED.items():
    text = (PERF / fname).read_text()
    defs = re.findall(rf"pub\(crate\) fn {re.escape(name)}\b", text)
    if len(defs) != 1:
        fail(f"{fname}: expected exactly 1 `pub(crate) fn {name}`, got {len(defs)}")
    print(f"  {fname}: pub(crate) fn {name} defined {len(defs)}x")

# ---- 5. check-ID uniqueness -------------------------------------------------
print("== check ID placement ==")
ids = re.findall(r'CheckMeta \{ id: "([A-Z0-9]+)"', mod_text)
print(f"  CHECKS table IDs: {len(ids)}")
check_files = sorted(PERF.glob("check_*.rs"))
for cid in ids:
    owners = []
    for cf in check_files:
        if f'"{cid}"' in cf.read_text():
            owners.append(cf.name)
    if len(owners) > 1:
        fail(f"check {cid} implemented in multiple files: {owners}")
    if cid in ("AGROW", "SAGROW", "PFBNS"):
        if owners:
            fail(f"file-level check {cid} should stay in mod.rs only, found in {owners}")
        print(f"  {cid}: mod.rs (file-level) [ok]")
    else:
        if len(owners) != 1:
            fail(f"node-level check {cid} must be implemented in exactly one check_*.rs, got {owners}")
        else:
            print(f"  {cid}: {owners[0]} [ok]")

# ---- 6. test counts and body fidelity ---------------------------------------
print("== test counts ==")
orig_tests = len(re.findall(r"^    fn ", "\n".join(orig_lines[1214:]), re.M))
mod_tests = len(re.findall(r"^    fn ", mod_text, re.M))
moved_total = 0
for cf in check_files:
    cnt = len(re.findall(r"^    fn ", cf.read_text(), re.M))
    moved_total += cnt
    print(f"  {cf.name}: {cnt} tests")
print(f"  original total: {orig_tests}, mod.rs: {mod_tests}, moved sum: {moved_total}")
if orig_tests != 81 or mod_tests != 7 or moved_total != 74:
    fail(f"test count mismatch: original={orig_tests} mod={mod_tests} moved={moved_total}")

# ---- 7. test body fidelity --------------------------------------------------
print("== test body fidelity ==")
# extract tests from original and from each new file; compare
def extract_tests(src_lines):
    out = {}
    i = 0
    while i < len(src_lines):
        if src_lines[i] == "    #[test]":
            j = i + 1
            m = re.match(r"^    fn (\w+)", src_lines[j])
            if m:
                name = m.group(1)
                close = None
                depth = 0
                for k in range(j, len(src_lines)):
                    if src_lines[k] == "    }":
                        close = k
                        break
                out[name] = "\n".join(src_lines[i:close + 1])
                i = close + 1
                continue
        i += 1
    return out

orig_tests_map = extract_tests(orig_lines)
new_tests_map = {}
for cf in check_files:
    new_tests_map.update(extract_tests(cf.read_text().split("\n")))
mod_tests_map = extract_tests(mod_text.split("\n"))
new_tests_map.update(mod_tests_map)
mismatch = 0
for name, body in orig_tests_map.items():
    if name not in new_tests_map:
        fail(f"test {name} missing after split")
        continue
    if new_tests_map[name] != body:
        fail(f"test {name} body changed")
        mismatch += 1
extra = set(new_tests_map) - set(orig_tests_map)
if extra:
    fail(f"unexpected new tests: {extra}")
print(f"  original tests: {len(orig_tests_map)}, after split: {len(new_tests_map)}, "
      f"body mismatches: {mismatch}")

# ---- 8. impl Rule block, CHECKS, inventory verbatim -------------------------
print("== structural blocks ==")
for label, pattern in [
    ("CHECKS table", r"const CHECKS:.*?\n\];"),
    ("impl Rule", r"impl Rule for PerformanceEngine \{.*?\n\}"),
    ("inventory::submit!", r"inventory::submit!\(.*?\n\);"),
]:
    m_orig = re.search(pattern, ORIG.read_text(), re.DOTALL)
    m_new = re.search(pattern, mod_text, re.DOTALL)
    ok = m_orig and m_new and m_orig.group(0) == m_new.group(0)
    print(f"  {label}: {'identical' if ok else 'DIFFERS'}")
    if not ok:
        fail(f"{label} differs")

# ---- summary ----------------------------------------------------------------
print()
if failures:
    print("FAILURES:")
    for f_ in failures:
        print("  -", f_.split("\n")[0][:200])
    sys.exit(1)
print("ALL VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED")
